paraphrase: In the first hymn the word 'Agni' primarily names Janārdana: 'agni' because he is foremost (agra) and leads (nī); as Bādarāyaṇa has explained, words such as Agni apply (primarily) to Janārdana.
speaker: Madhva

paraphrase: Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa, full of all qualities, free of defects, lord of all, the meaning of the Ṛks is told. Om designates him as the support of all qualities; he is the meaning of the Gāyatrī as the impeller of all intellects and the Puruṣa of the Puruṣa-sūkta; he alone is the meaning of all the Vedas, of all śāstras and of all words, as the supreme Upaniṣad says.
speaker: Madhva
